security_audit.summary: The static command, network, and filesystem findings are false positives from Markdown examples, documentation links, and normal Nx configuration paths. A semantic review found one medium credential-handling risk because the remote cache example shows token placeholders inside nx.json.

remediation.issue: Remote cache examples show access tokens in shared Nx configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Use environment variables or CI secret references, and state that real Nx Cloud tokens must not be committed.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Handling Risk in Remote Cache Example
semantic_findings.description: The remote caching example places Nx Cloud token placeholders inside nx.json. Users may copy this pattern and commit real access tokens to source control.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file uses placeholder token values, not real secrets, but the example location is a shared configuration file. This creates a plausible unsafe copy-paste pattern.

content.value_statement: Nx monorepos can become slow and hard to govern without clear boundaries and cache rules. This skill provides templates for project structure, affected commands, CI, generators, and remote caching.
actual_capabilities: Explains Nx workspace structure for apps, libraries, tools, and shared code.
Provides nx.json templates for target defaults, named inputs, cacheable operations, and generators.
Shows module boundary rules using project tags and dependency constraints.
Includes a custom feature library generator example for Nx React projects.
Outlines CI affected commands and remote caching configuration patterns.
limitations: Does not inspect a repository automatically without user-provided files or command output.
Examples may need updates for the installed Nx version and plugins.
Remote cache setup still requires secure token management outside the skill.
It does not replace official Nx migration guidance for major upgrades.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Monorepo
use_cases.description: Design an Nx workspace layout with apps, libraries, tags, and ownership boundaries before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Reduce CI Runtime
use_cases.description: Adopt affected commands, caching, and parallel task settings to reduce redundant lint, test, build, and e2e work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Library Boundaries
use_cases.description: Create consistent feature, UI, data-access, and utility layers with enforceable dependency constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workspace Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design an Nx workspace for [apps] and [shared libraries]. Include project layout, tags, and initial commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add Module Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Nx project list and propose enforce-module-boundaries rules for app, feature, ui, data-access, and util layers.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Affected CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow for this Nx repository that uses affected lint, test, build, and e2e tasks with caching.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Generator Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom Nx generator for feature libraries in [framework]. Include options, tags, file placement, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I need a workspace for web, api, and shared UI libraries.
output_examples.output: A workspace plan with apps under apps, shared utilities under libs/shared, feature libraries under scope folders, and consistent project tags.

output_examples.input: Our CI runs every test for every pull request.
output_examples.output: A CI strategy that uses affected lint, test, build, and e2e tasks, with cacheable targets and controlled parallelism.

output_examples.input: Developers import across layers without rules.
output_examples.output: A boundary model that separates app, feature, UI, data-access, and utility layers with clear dependency constraints.

best_practices: Define project tags before writing boundary rules.
Enable local and CI caching early, then measure affected command results.
Keep feature libraries focused and generate them consistently.
anti_patterns: Do not commit service tokens inside nx.json or other shared config files.
Do not bypass module boundary rules to fix short-term import problems.
Do not create many tiny libraries without ownership or build value.

faq.question: Can this skill create an Nx workspace?
faq.answer: It can guide setup steps and templates. The user or agent must still run the appropriate Nx commands.

faq.question: Does it support Nx Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes, it explains remote cache patterns. Tokens should be managed with environment variables or repository secrets.

faq.question: Can it review my current nx.json?
faq.answer: Yes, provide the file contents or repository context and ask for targeted improvements.

faq.question: Is it only for React?
faq.answer: No. Some examples use React, but the workspace and boundary patterns apply across Nx plugins.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command examples and verification steps for the user or coding agent to choose.

faq.question: Does it replace official Nx documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use official documentation for version-specific options and migrations.
